title: IA Agents and the Humanities: What Changes When the Machine Writes With Us?

yaml.title: IA Agents and the Humanities: What Changes When the Machine Writes With Us?
yaml.author: Ricardo Sodré Andrade
yaml.description: A reflection on how AI agents are transforming the practice of digital humanities.

markdown.markdown:
When we speak of "digital humanities," we usually think of applying
computational tools to humanistic problems. But AI agents invert this
relationship: it is no longer us who apply the machine to texts — it is
the machine that is reading, interpreting, and responding to our texts
in ways that challenge our traditional categories.

An AI agent is not just an advanced search tool. It plans, decides,
executes, and learns. In the context of the humanities, this means that
the agent can identify patterns in documentary collections that a human
researcher would take years to perceive — but it can also reproduce
biases present in training data in subtle and hard-to-detect ways.

## Between tool and interlocutor

There is a fundamental difference between using text analysis software and
working with an agent that converses, proposes, questions. In the first
case, the researcher maintains epistemic control: they formulate the
question and the machine answers. In the second, the agent can reframe
the question, suggest unexplored paths, or even disagree.

This is not necessarily a problem. It can be productively challenging. But
it requires us to rethink what "authorship" means in a text produced in
collaboration with an AI agent.

## What remains, what changes

Archival practice, for example, has clear rules of description and
provenance. An AI agent can help describe entire documentary fonds in
hours, but human validation remains necessary — not out of distrust, but
because archival description is an interpretive act, not merely
classificatory.

Enhanced is born from this unease: a space to think, in free text, about
what it means to do humanities when artificial intelligence has ceased to
be a tool and has become an interlocutor.

---

the blog post and the academic essay, accessible yet rigorous.*
